*From C99, the first standard after the second edition of Kernighan and Ritchie.*

| You will read | What it is | Where the book teaches it |
|---|---|---|
| `int32_t` | A signed integer of exactly 32 bits, from `<stdint.h>`, so a word means the same on every target. | Used throughout; ch01 says why a word's width matters. |
| `uint32_t` | An unsigned integer of exactly 32 bits, from `<stdint.h>`. | Used throughout. |
| `int64_t` | A signed integer of exactly 64 bits, from `<stdint.h>`: the width of a tagged pointer. | ch17, where a pointer and a tag share one word. |
| `static inline` | A function defined in a header, visible only in the file that includes it, which the compiler may expand in place rather than call. | The barrier and the wait in `cm.h`; ch02 and ch06. |
| `for (int i = 0; ...)` | A loop variable declared in the loop header, where C89 required every declaration at the top of a block. | Every kernel's `cm_run`. |
